nodes.description: PHLDB1 encodes pleckstrin homology-like domain family B member 1, a protein with a reported normal role in insulin-dependent Akt phosphorylation that has not yet been tested in OI type XXIII patient cells. In OI type XXIII, biallelic frameshift variants reduce PHLDB1 mRNA expression in blood and skin fibroblasts and abolish PHLDB1 protein on western blot of cultured patient fibroblasts. This loss of PHLDB1 is the proximal molecular lesion; the downstream pathway by which it impairs bone formation and matrix strength is not yet established.

nodes.description: Loss of PHLDB1 produces a mild OI phenotype with recurrent fractures and/or osteopenia together with characteristic spondylometaphyseal changes (platyspondyly, short and bowed long bones, widened metaphyses) that characteristically regress after early childhood. Because the molecular link between PHLDB1 loss and the bone matrix defect has not been established, the mechanism connecting the proximal lesion to the skeletal phenotype is represented at the tissue-level bone-formation and skeletal-fragility scale.
